description: ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret default in Dockerfile build args; literal 'secret' is baked into image layers when build-arg is not overridden, becoming session-signing secret.
ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret default — master AES-256-CBC credential-encryption key falls back to literal 'secret' baked into image layers if not overridden.
Hardcoded POSTGRES_PASSWORD=magical_password committed in docker-compose.yml database service env block — default DB credential present in repository history.
Default org-user password derived as createHash('md5').update(email + CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY).digest('hex') — fast MD5 of predictable inputs enables offline brute-force.
uses: lingodotdev/lingo.dev@main pins a third-party action to a mutable branch and runs with a GitHub App token (contents:write, pull-requests:write) — supply-chain risk.
Dockerfile starts FROM node:20 and never issues a USER directive — final image runs CMD as root, granting unnecessary privilege to the running app.
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' set alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: 'true' (line 9) on every API v1 response — overly permissive CORS configuration.
Production script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' and https: alongside 'strict-dynamic' as legacy-browser fallback — older clients see weakened policy permitting inline scripts.
Static Content-Security-Policy header includes 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in script-src and 'unsafe-inline' in style-src — defeats CSP XSS protection.
shouldEnforceCsp restricts CSP header emission to /auth/login and /login paths — all other routes (including authenticated dashboards) have no Content-Security-Policy.
Open redirect: return-to cookie value is used unsanitized in NextResponse.redirect(new URL(returnTo.value, req.url)) on /apps/installed routes.
HitPay webhook HMAC comparison uses signed !== obj.hmac (non-constant-time string equality) instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual — observable-timing side channel.
log.debug('CredentialsProvider:credentials:authorize', safeStringify({ credentials })) logs the full credentials object (including password) at debug level.
TOTP secret = createHash('md5').update(email + (CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '')).digest('hex') — MD5 is cryptographically broken and empty-key fallback compounds weakness.
Email-verification TOTP secret = createHash('md5').update(email + CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY).digest('hex') — MD5 unsuitable as cryptographic seed for one-time codes.
clientSecretVerifier = process.env.SAML_CLIENT_SECRET_VERIFIER || 'dummy' — SAML OIDC client-secret verifier defaults to literal 'dummy' string when env unset.
fetch(subscriberUrl, ...) dispatches outbound webhook to user-supplied subscriberUrl without SSRF allow-list, IP filter, or DNS-rebind protection.
symmetricEncrypt uses AES-256-CBC (createCipheriv('aes256', ...)) with no MAC/HMAC — unauthenticated cipher vulnerable to padding-oracle and bit-flip ciphertext attacks.
Buffer.from(key, 'latin1') decodes the AES key as Latin1 bytes — a 32-char ASCII key keeps 256 bits but UTF-8 keys are silently truncated, reducing effective entropy.
getIP trusts cf-connecting-ip and x-real-ip headers without verifying request actually came through Cloudflare/proxy — direct clients can spoof source IP.
Organization invite code verification derives TOTP secret as MD5(email + CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) — broken hash for sensitive org-membership flow.
Workflow email-verification TOTP secret = createHash('md5').update(email + CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY).digest('hex') — broken hash function for cryptographic seed.
Hardcoded POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 'magical_password' in workflow env block — used by ephemeral CI Postgres but commits a weak literal credential into VCS.
NestJS API v2 Dockerfile lacks USER directive — CMD ['yarn', 'workspace', '@calcom/api-v2', 'start:prod'] runs as root inside the production container.
When ALLOWED_ORIGINS env unset and NODE_ENV !== 'production', enableCors falls back to origin: '*' — permissive CORS if env misconfigured in non-prod deploys.
jwt.verify(token, encryptionKey) lacks an algorithms allow-list — accepts any HMAC variant the library defaults to; pin algorithms: ['HS256'] to harden against alg-confusion attacks.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML interpolates ${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID} into inline GTM init script body — malformed env value can break out of the script context.
POST /api/router preflight and POST handlers set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' — unrestricted cross-origin access to routing-forms router endpoint.
Hardcoded POSTGRES_USER=unicorn_user committed in docker-compose.yml — paired with magical_password creates well-known default DB credential set.
RawHtml React component injects caller-supplied html prop via dangerouslySetInnerHTML using </script>${html}<script> breakout — XSS sink if html is not sanitised.
jwt.verify(token, secret) lacks an explicit algorithms allow-list — accepts any HMAC variant the library defaults to; pin algorithms: ['HS256'] to harden against future key/alg changes.
CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is reused as AES-256-CBC symmetric key (lib/crypto.ts) and as JWT HMAC secret here — single key shared across distinct cryptographic algorithms.
verifyRefreshToken calls jwt.verify(refreshToken, secretKey) without an algorithms allow-list — accepts any default HMAC variant; pin algorithms: ['HS256'] to prevent alg-confusion.
createWebhookSignature returns '' when params.secret is null/empty so X-Cal-Signature-256 header is omitted — subscriber cannot authenticate the payload.
Minimum password length is 7 (if password.length >= 7 ...) for non-strict mode — below NIST SP 800-63B recommended minimum of 8 characters.
rateLimiter() fails open when UNKEY_ROOT_KEY is unset — returns {success:true,...} for every request, silently disabling all 8 rate-limit namespaces (auth, sms, api, core, etc).
Md5PiiHasher hashes email PII with FNV-1a 32-bit (chained 4x for 128 bits) — non-cryptographic hash provides no pre-image resistance against rainbow attacks.
Workflow references actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 by mutable major-version tags rather than pinning to immutable commit SHAs.
Fallback xff ? parseIpFromHeaders(xff) : '127.0.0.1' — when no IP header is present, all anonymous callers share one rate-limit identifier.
